title: Token on its own line between the delimiter lines of a multiline environment-file record
summary: A synthetic ghs_ installation token on its own line between the delimiter lines of a multiline GITHUB_ENV or GITHUB_OUTPUT record (NAME<<DELIMITER, the value, DELIMITER), with a fixed EOF delimiter and with a random-identifier delimiter.
rationale: In the multiline form the name and the value are not on one line: the name sits on the opening line with <<DELIMITER, the value follows on the next line, and a closing line repeats the delimiter. The documentation's own PowerShell example generates the delimiter as a GUID, so one of the three lines can look like a credential-sized identifier while being only framing. The reported range is the value line alone: not the opening line, not the delimiter, not the closing line.

expectation.rationale: Flagged. The value between the delimiter lines is the record's value and holds a token of the documented family; the delimiter lines are framing that the documentation says must not occur on a line of its own within the value, and carry no secret.

sources.supports: Multiline strings use {name}<<{delimiter}, then {value}, then {delimiter}; the delimiter must not occur on a line of its own within the value; the PowerShell example generates the delimiter with New-Guid.
An output parameter can be set to a multi-line value with the same technique used for multi-line environment variables.
Format of the ghs_ token family (opaque form of 40 characters; the staged rollout of the ghs_APPID_JWT form).

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04, before any scanner was consulted. Origin of the inputs: the command shapes are taken from the cited documentation examples (observed); the token is a synthetic value built from an existing authored base; the arrangement of one value in each command shape is evidence-derived, not an observed workflow. No workflow was executed and no value was tested. Whether a consumer reads a workflow file, an environment file or a runner log, and how it treats a mask, is the consumer's measurement contract and is not assumed here. The GUID delimiter is a synthetic, obviously fake identifier built from an authored description (all-zero groups with a synthetic marker), not a captured value.
